entries.meaning: An animal with feathers, two wings, and a beak. ---
examples: A bird hit the window and knocked itself out.
There were hundreds of birds sitting on the wire outside.
She keeps a bird in a cage by the kitchen window.

entries.meaning: Eagle has 2 distinct senses.
examples: An eagle circled over the canyon for almost an hour.
Two bald eagles nest on the island every spring.
The eagle dropped out of the sky and grabbed a fish.
He sank a long putt for an eagle on the par five.
Two eagles in one round is almost unheard of.
Her eagle on the sixteenth won the tournament.

senses.head: A large bird of prey with a hooked beak and very good eyesight
examples: An eagle circled over the canyon for almost an hour.
Two bald eagles nest on the island every spring.
The eagle dropped out of the sky and grabbed a fish.

senses.head: A golf score of two strokes under par on one hole
examples: He sank a long putt for an eagle on the par five.
Two eagles in one round is almost unheard of.
Her eagle on the sixteenth won the tournament.

entries.русский: орёл; игл (на два удара ниже пара)

entries.meaning: Hawk has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A hawk was sitting on the fence post, watching the field.
Hawks around here go after squirrels and rabbits.
We saw a red-tailed hawk on the drive up.
The hawks in Congress pushed for airstrikes.
He was a hawk on the deficit and voted against every spending bill.
The president's advisers split into hawks and doves.

senses.head: A medium-sized bird of prey that hunts small animals by day
examples: A hawk was sitting on the fence post, watching the field.
Hawks around here go after squirrels and rabbits.
We saw a red-tailed hawk on the drive up.

senses.head: Someone who supports military force or a tough, aggressive policy
examples: The hawks in Congress pushed for airstrikes.
He was a hawk on the deficit and voted against every spending bill.
The president's advisers split into hawks and doves.

entries.meaning: A fast bird of prey with long pointed wings. ---
examples: A falcon can dive faster than any other bird.
The city has a pair of falcons nesting on the courthouse.
He trained the falcon to come back to his glove.

entries.meaning: A night bird with large forward-facing eyes and a flat face. ---
examples: An owl was hooting somewhere behind the barn.
Owls hunt at night, so you rarely see them.
We found an owl pellet under the big pine.

entries.meaning: Vulture has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A couple of vultures were circling over the highway.
The vulture waited until the coyote left.
Vultures clean up carcasses that would otherwise rot.
Vultures moved into the neighborhood after the flood, buying homes cheap.
Investors circled the failing company like vultures.
He called the payday lenders vultures.

senses.head: A large bird that feeds on dead animals
examples: A couple of vultures were circling over the highway.
The vulture waited until the coyote left.
Vultures clean up carcasses that would otherwise rot.

senses.head: A person who takes advantage of other people's troubles for profit
examples: Vultures moved into the neighborhood after the flood, buying homes cheap.
Investors circled the failing company like vultures.
He called the payday lenders vultures.

entries.русский: гриф, стервятник; стервятник (наживающийся на чужой беде)

entries.meaning: A large black bird with a harsh call. ---
examples: A crow landed on the mailbox and stared at me.
Crows remember faces, which is a little unsettling.
The crow dropped a walnut on the road so a car would crack it.

entries.meaning: A large black bird like a crow but bigger, with a deeper call. ---
examples: A raven is much bigger than a crow, and its call is deeper.
Ravens nested on the cliff above the trail.
The raven followed us for half a mile, hoping for scraps.

entries.meaning: A small brown and gray bird common in towns and gardens. ---
examples: A sparrow built a nest in the gutter.
Sparrows were fighting over crumbs on the patio.
There is always a sparrow or two under the feeder.

entries.meaning: A gray city bird with a small head and a fat body. ---
examples: A pigeon was walking around the subway platform.
The old man feeds the pigeons in the square every morning.
A pigeon got into the warehouse and could not find its way out.
entries.contrast: Two syllables, not three: PIJ-un, never pi-JEE-on. The g is soft.

entries.meaning: Dove has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A dove landed on the windowsill and cooed.
Two white doves were released at the wedding.
The dove is a symbol of peace in a lot of countries.
The debate split the cabinet into hawks and doves.
He was known as a dove on foreign policy.
Even the doves voted for the sanctions.

senses.head: A small pale pigeon, often used as a symbol of peace
examples: A dove landed on the windowsill and cooed.
Two white doves were released at the wedding.
The dove is a symbol of peace in a lot of countries.

senses.head: A politician or official who prefers peace and negotiation to force
examples: The debate split the cabinet into hawks and doves.
He was known as a dove on foreign policy.
Even the doves voted for the sanctions.

entries.contrast: The bird rhymes with love: /dʌv/. The identically spelled past tense of dive is /doʊv/, rhyming with stove.

entries.meaning: A common garden bird with a red or orange breast. ---
examples: A robin was pulling a worm out of the lawn.
Robins show up in the yard as soon as the ground thaws.
We watched a robin feed her chicks all afternoon.

entries.meaning: A large white water bird with a long curved neck. ---
examples: A swan glided past us without making a sound.
Two swans have nested on the lake for years.
The swan hissed when we got too close to the nest.
entries.contrast: The a is /ɑː/: SWAHN rhymes with on, not with man.

entries.meaning: A flightless black and white sea bird of the southern hemisphere. ---
examples: The zoo just opened a new penguin exhibit.
Penguins cannot fly, but they swim beautifully.
A penguin waddled up to the glass and stared at my son.

entries.meaning: A very large flightless African bird that runs fast. ---
examples: An ostrich can outrun a horse over open ground.
They raise ostriches on a farm outside of town.
The ostrich laid an egg the size of a football.

entries.meaning: A brightly colored tropical bird with a curved beak that can copy speech. ---
examples: Their parrot says hello every time the doorbell rings.
Parrots can live for fifty years or more.
The parrot bit my finger when I got too close.

entries.meaning: A small parrot with a long tail, often kept as a pet. ---
examples: She keeps two parakeets in a cage by the window.
The parakeet escaped and spent the night on the curtain rod.
A green parakeet was chirping in the pet store.

entries.meaning: A large parrot with a crest that it can raise on its head. ---
examples: The cockatoo raised its crest when the dog walked in.
Cockatoos are loud enough to wake the neighbors.
He taught his cockatoo to whistle the theme song.

entries.meaning: A big long-tailed parrot from Central and South America. ---
examples: A blue and gold macaw sat on the trainer's arm.
Macaws need a lot of space and a lot of attention.
The macaw screamed every time the phone rang.
entries.contrast: Stress falls on the second syllable: muh-KAW.

entries.meaning: A male bird with a huge fan-shaped tail of blue and green feathers. ---
examples: A peacock spread its tail right in front of the tourists.
Peacocks wander loose all over the hotel grounds.
The peacock let out that awful cry at five in the morning.

entries.meaning: A gray and white sea bird common along coasts. ---
examples: A seagull stole a fry right out of my hand.
The seagulls follow the fishing boats back into the harbor.
One seagull landed on the roof of the car.

entries.meaning: A sea bird of the same family as the seagull. ---
examples: A gull was riding the wind over the pier.
Gulls nest on the rocks at the end of the beach.
The gull dropped a clam on the parking lot to break it open.

entries.meaning: A tall wading bird with long legs and a long straight bill. ---
examples: A stork was standing in the shallow water.
Storks nest on chimneys in a lot of old towns.
In the old story, a stork brings the baby.

entries.meaning: Crane has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A crane took off from the marsh as we drove by.
Thousands of cranes stop here on their way south.
The crane stood on one leg for almost ten minutes.
A crane lifted the steel beams onto the roof.
Three cranes stood over the half-built tower.
The crane operator worked from a cab a hundred feet up.

senses.head: A tall long-necked bird that lives in wetlands
examples: A crane took off from the marsh as we drove by.
Thousands of cranes stop here on their way south.
The crane stood on one leg for almost ten minutes.

senses.head: A tall machine with a long arm for lifting heavy loads
examples: A crane lifted the steel beams onto the roof.
Three cranes stood over the half-built tower.
The crane operator worked from a cab a hundred feet up.

entries.contrast: The same word also means a lifting machine on a building site; only context tells you which.

entries.meaning: A wading bird with long legs and a sharp bill that spears fish. ---
examples: A blue heron was standing dead still at the edge of the pond.
Herons nest in the tall trees along the river.
The heron speared a fish and swallowed it whole.

entries.meaning: A large water bird with a pouch under its bill for holding fish. ---
examples: A pelican dove straight into the surf.
Pelicans line up on the railing at the end of the pier.
The pelican had a fish flopping around in its pouch.

entries.meaning: Swallow has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A swallow built a mud nest under the eaves.
Swallows come back to the barn every April.
The swallow caught a bug in midair.
He took a long swallow of coffee.
There were only a few swallows left in the bottle.
She washed the pill down with a swallow of water.

senses.head: A small fast bird with pointed wings and a forked tail
examples: A swallow built a mud nest under the eaves.
Swallows come back to the barn every April.
The swallow caught a bug in midair.

senses.head: An amount of food or drink taken down the throat at one time
examples: He took a long swallow of coffee.
There were only a few swallows left in the bottle.
She washed the pill down with a swallow of water.

entries.contrast: Spelled and said exactly like the verb swallow (to send food down your throat).

entries.meaning: A bird that hammers holes in trees with its beak to find insects. ---
examples: A woodpecker has been hammering on the siding since dawn.
Woodpeckers drill holes to get at insects under the bark.
The woodpecker left a row of neat holes in the dead tree.

entries.meaning: A tiny bird that hovers in front of flowers and beats its wings very fast. ---
examples: A hummingbird hovered at the feeder for a few seconds.
Hummingbirds beat their wings so fast you can barely see them.
We put out sugar water to bring the hummingbirds in.

entries.meaning: A small yellow songbird often kept in a cage. ---
examples: Their canary sings all morning.
Miners used to carry canaries down into the shafts.
The canary stopped singing when we turned on the vacuum.
entries.contrast: Stress on the middle syllable: kuh-NAIR-ee, not CAN-uh-ree.

entries.meaning: A small seed-eating songbird with a short thick beak. ---
examples: A finch was picking seeds off the ground.
Finches took over the feeder by the garage.
The little yellow finch comes back every summer.

entries.meaning: A small bright yellow finch with black markings. ---
examples: A goldfinch landed on the thistle feeder.
Goldfinches turn bright yellow in the spring.
We counted six goldfinches in the yard this morning.

entries.meaning: A small brown bird famous for singing at night. ---
examples: A nightingale was singing somewhere in the dark.
Nightingales are famous for their song, not their looks.
He said the nightingale kept him awake half the night.

entries.meaning: A bird that lays its eggs in other birds' nests and calls its own name. ---
examples: A cuckoo was calling from the woods.
Cuckoos lay their eggs in other birds' nests.
The clock has a little wooden cuckoo that pops out on the hour.

entries.meaning: A noisy black and white bird with a long tail. ---
examples: A magpie carried off a piece of foil from the trash.
Magpies are smart enough to recognize themselves in a mirror.
The magpie sat on the fence, chattering at the cat.

entries.meaning: A dark speckled bird that flies in huge flocks and copies other sounds. ---
examples: A starling was picking at the grass by the curb.
Thousands of starlings wheeled over the field at dusk.
The starling can imitate a car alarm almost perfectly.

entries.meaning: A loud, bold bird of the crow family, often blue in North America. ---
examples: A blue jay chased the squirrel off the feeder.
Jays scream when there is a hawk around.
The jay buried an acorn in the flower bed.

entries.meaning: A common black songbird. ---
examples: A blackbird was singing on the fence post.
Blackbirds fill the marsh in the spring.
The blackbird flew off as soon as I opened the door.

entries.meaning: A small North American songbird with bright blue feathers. ---
examples: A bluebird took over the box we put up last year.
Bluebirds are back, so spring must be close.
The bluebird sat on the wire for a long time.

entries.meaning: A North American songbird; the male is bright red with a crest. ---
examples: A male cardinal is impossible to miss against the snow.
Cardinals come to the feeder all winter.
The cardinal was singing from the top of the maple.

entries.meaning: A very small brown bird with a short upright tail and a loud song. ---
examples: A wren built a nest in the flowerpot.
Wrens are tiny, but they are unbelievably loud.
The wren scolded me the whole time I was on the porch.
entries.contrast: The w is silent: REN, one syllable.

entries.meaning: Lark has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A lark rose straight up over the field, singing.
Larks nest right on the ground.
We heard a lark long before we saw it.
We drove to the coast on a lark.
He entered the contest as a lark and won.
What started as a lark turned into a real business.

senses.head: A brown field bird that sings while flying high in the air
examples: A lark rose straight up over the field, singing.
Larks nest right on the ground.
We heard a lark long before we saw it.

senses.head: Something done just for fun or on a sudden whim
examples: We drove to the coast on a lark.
He entered the contest as a lark and won.
What started as a lark turned into a real business.

entries.meaning: A brightly colored bird that dives into water to catch fish. ---
examples: A kingfisher was perched on a branch over the creek.
Kingfishers hunt by dropping straight into the water.
The kingfisher rattled as it flew downstream.

entries.meaning: A small black and white sea bird with a large brightly striped bill. ---
examples: We took a boat out to see the puffins.
A puffin landed with three fish in its beak.
Puffins nest in burrows on the cliffs.

entries.meaning: A very large sea bird with long narrow wings that glides for hours. ---
examples: An albatross followed the ship for two days.
Albatrosses can glide for hours without flapping.
The albatross has the longest wingspan of any bird.

entries.meaning: A very large vulture of the American mountains. ---
examples: A wild condor passed right over the canyon rim.
There were only a couple dozen condors left in the wild.
The condor is slowly coming back from near extinction.

entries.meaning: A broad-winged bird of prey; in American usage often a vulture. ---
examples: A buzzard was picking at something on the shoulder of the road.
Buzzards were circling over the field all afternoon.
The buzzard took off when the truck came around the bend.
entries.contrast: In American English a buzzard is usually a vulture; in British English it is a kind of hawk.

entries.meaning: A large fish-eating bird of prey found near water. ---
examples: An osprey dropped feet first into the lake and came up with a fish.
Ospreys build huge nests on top of power poles.
The osprey has been fishing this stretch of river all summer.

entries.meaning: A large flightless Australian bird, second in height only to the ostrich. ---
examples: An emu got loose from the farm and walked down the highway.
Emus are the second tallest birds in the world.
The emu pecked at my shoelaces.

entries.meaning: A tropical American bird with an enormous colorful bill. ---
examples: A toucan landed in the tree above our table.
Toucans use that huge bill to reach fruit on thin branches.
The toucan tossed the berry into the air and caught it.
entries.contrast: Sounds like the words two can: TOO-kan.

entries.meaning: An adult male chicken. ---
examples: The rooster starts crowing around four in the morning.
They keep one rooster and a dozen hens.
Two roosters in the same pen is asking for a fight.
entries.contrast: American English says rooster; British English usually says cock or cockerel.

entries.meaning: An adult female chicken, or the female of some other birds. ---
examples: One hen is laying an egg almost every day.
The hens got out and were all over the driveway.
A hen will sit on the eggs for about three weeks.

entries.meaning: Chick has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A chick poked its head out of the shell.
All twelve chicks hatched over two days.
The mother bird kept bringing worms back to the chick.
Some chick from accounting left you a note.
He calls every woman a chick, and nobody appreciates it.
A couple of chicks in the front row started laughing.

senses.head: A very young bird, especially a young chicken
examples: A chick poked its head out of the shell.
All twelve chicks hatched over two days.
The mother bird kept bringing worms back to the chick.

senses.head: An informal and often disrespectful word for a young woman
examples: Some chick from accounting left you a note.
He calls every woman a chick, and nobody appreciates it.
A couple of chicks in the front row started laughing.

entries.русский: птенец, цыплёнок; девчонка, тёлка (разг., часто пренебрежительно)

entries.meaning: A young duck. ---
examples: A duckling was trailing behind the others.
Nine ducklings followed their mother into the water.
The duckling was all fuzz and feet.

entries.meaning: A young goose. ---
examples: A gosling was grazing on the lawn by the pond.
The geese hissed whenever anyone got near the goslings.
That gosling is almost as big as its parents now.
entries.contrast: The o is /ɑː/, not the /uː/ of goose: GAHZ-ling.

entries.meaning: A young swan. ---
examples: A cygnet is gray for the first year.
The pair had five cygnets riding on their backs.
The cygnet stayed close to its mother the whole time.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like signet (a signet ring): the c is /s/ and the g is hard.

entries.meaning: A male duck. ---
examples: The drake has the green head; the female is brown.
Two drakes were chasing each other across the pond.
A drake landed in the decoys about twenty yards out.

entries.meaning: Gander has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The gander hissed and came at me with his neck out.
One gander can guard a whole yard.
The ganders were fighting over territory by the water.
Take a gander at this photo.
Let me have a gander at the menu.
He stopped to take a gander at the car in the driveway.

senses.head: A male goose
examples: The gander hissed and came at me with his neck out.
One gander can guard a whole yard.
The ganders were fighting over territory by the water.

senses.head: A quick look at something
examples: Take a gander at this photo.
Let me have a gander at the menu.
He stopped to take a gander at the car in the driveway.

entries.meaning: A gray North American songbird that imitates other birds and sounds. ---
examples: A mockingbird sang outside my window until two in the morning.
Mockingbirds can copy car alarms and cell phones.
The mockingbird dive-bombed the cat.

entries.meaning: A small North American bird with a black cap, named for its call. ---
examples: A chickadee grabbed one seed and flew off with it.
Chickadees stay all winter, even in the cold.
The chickadee landed right on my hand.

entries.meaning: Loon has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A loon called out across the lake at sunset.
Loons dive and stay under for a surprisingly long time.
We watched a loon carry its chick on its back.
The guy on the corner is a harmless loon.
You'd have to be a loon to swim in that water.
A few loons showed up in shorts in January.

senses.head: A diving water bird of northern lakes with a haunting call
examples: A loon called out across the lake at sunset.
Loons dive and stay under for a surprisingly long time.
We watched a loon carry its chick on its back.

senses.head: A silly or crazy person
examples: The guy on the corner is a harmless loon.
You'd have to be a loon to swim in that water.
A few loons showed up in shorts in January.

entries.meaning: A large flightless bird that died out in the seventeenth century. ---
examples: The dodo has been extinct for over three hundred years.
Dodos had no natural predators until sailors arrived.
The museum has a model of a dodo in the entryway.

entries.meaning: A bird that lives on or near the ocean. ---
examples: A seabird was riding the wind above the cliffs.
Seabirds nest by the thousands on that island.
The oil spill killed every seabird along the coast.

entries.meaning: A bird known for its musical call. ---
examples: A songbird woke us up at first light.
Songbirds are disappearing from a lot of the country.
The cat has killed more than one songbird this summer.

entries.meaning: A bird that swims and lives on water, such as a duck or a goose. ---
examples: The refuge protects waterfowl on their way south.
A single waterfowl was left on the frozen pond.
Hunting waterfowl here requires a separate permit.
entries.contrast: The plural is normally waterfowl, unchanged — not waterfowls.

entries.meaning: A bird kept for meat and eggs, or a wild bird hunted for food. ---
examples: The pond was full of wild fowl.
They keep a few fowl out behind the barn.
The recipe works with any kind of fowl.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like foul (unfair, disgusting), and the plural is usually fowl, unchanged.

entries.meaning: Raptor has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A raptor was perched on the light pole over the interstate.
Raptors have hooked beaks and very sharp talons.
The center takes in injured raptors and releases them.
The kids wanted to see the raptors at the natural history museum.
A raptor had one long curved claw on each foot.
In the movie the raptors learn how to open doors.

senses.head: A bird that hunts other animals, such as a hawk, eagle, or owl
examples: A raptor was perched on the light pole over the interstate.
Raptors have hooked beaks and very sharp talons.
The center takes in injured raptors and releases them.

senses.head: A small, fast, meat-eating dinosaur
examples: The kids wanted to see the raptors at the natural history museum.
A raptor had one long curved claw on each foot.
In the movie the raptors learn how to open doors.

entries.meaning: A bird that kills and eats other animals. ---
examples: A bird of prey was working the field along the fence line.
Hawks, eagles, and owls are all birds of prey.
The bird of prey dropped on the mouse without a sound.
entries.contrast: The plural is birds of prey — the s goes on bird, not on prey.

entries.meaning: One of the light growths that cover a bird's body. ---
examples: A single feather drifted down onto the deck.
The pillow is stuffed with duck feathers.
She found a blue jay feather on the trail.
entries.contrast: The ea is short: FE-thur, rhyming with weather, not with either.

entries.meaning: The distance from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other. ---
examples: That eagle had a six-foot wingspan.
A condor has the biggest wingspan of any bird on the continent.
Their wingspans can reach almost ten feet.

entries.meaning: The hard pointed mouth part of a bird. ---
examples: The bird had a worm in its beak.
Parrots crack seeds with their beaks.
It cleaned its feathers with the tip of its beak.

entries.meaning: Bill has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A duck's bill is flat and wide.
The pelican's bill holds more than its stomach does.
Some birds have long, curved bills for reaching into flowers.
Can you break a hundred-dollar bill?
The electric bill was huge this month.
We split the bill three ways.

senses.head: A bird's beak, especially a flat wide one
examples: A duck's bill is flat and wide.
The pelican's bill holds more than its stomach does.
Some birds have long, curved bills for reaching into flowers.

senses.head: A piece of paper money, or a statement of what you owe
examples: Can you break a hundred-dollar bill?
The electric bill was huge this month.
We split the bill three ways.

entries.русский: клюв (плоский, у водоплавающих); купюра; счёт к оплате
entries.contrast: The same word also means a bill you pay and, in American English, a banknote (a ten-dollar bill).

entries.meaning: A claw on a bird of prey. ---
examples: The hawk sank a talon into the rabbit.
Owls carry prey in their talons.
One talon was broken off at the tip.

entries.meaning: Crest has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The bird raised its crest when it got excited.
Cardinals have a pointed crest on the head.
Both crests went up the moment the dog appeared.
The house sits on the crest of the hill.
Surfers waited for the crest of the next wave.
You can see the ocean once you reach the crest.
The school crest is stitched on every blazer.
He wore a ring with his family crest.
Both team crests were painted at midfield.

senses.head: A tuft of feathers on top of a bird's head
examples: The bird raised its crest when it got excited.
Cardinals have a pointed crest on the head.
Both crests went up the moment the dog appeared.

senses.head: The highest part of a hill, a wave, or a rise in the road
examples: The house sits on the crest of the hill.
Surfers waited for the crest of the next wave.
You can see the ocean once you reach the crest.

senses.head: A design used as the emblem of a family, school, or team
examples: The school crest is stitched on every blazer.
He wore a ring with his family crest.
Both team crests were painted at midfield.

entries.русский: хохолок, гребень; гребень (волны), вершина (холма); герб, эмблема

entries.meaning: All the feathers covering a bird. ---
examples: The male's plumage is much brighter than the female's.
Winter plumage is duller and better for hiding.
Its plumage was still wet from the rain.
entries.contrast: Uncountable: bright plumage, never a plumage or plumages.

entries.meaning: Down has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The chicks are covered in soft gray down.
The jacket is filled with goose down.
Down is warmer than any synthetic filling.
It's third down and eight yards to go.
They picked up a first down on the next play.
The offense wasted two downs running out the clock.

senses.head: The soft fine feathers under a bird's outer feathers
examples: The chicks are covered in soft gray down.
The jacket is filled with goose down.
Down is warmer than any synthetic filling.

senses.head: In football, one of the four tries a team gets to advance the ball ten yards
examples: It's third down and eight yards to go.
They picked up a first down on the next play.
The offense wasted two downs running out the clock.

entries.contrast: Uncountable: some down, never a down or downs. Spelled like the direction word down.

entries.meaning: Quill has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A single quill had fallen out of the wing.
People used to write with goose quills.
The quill was stiff and hollow at the base.
The dog came home with quills in his nose.
A porcupine raises its quills when it feels threatened.
Each quill has a barbed tip that is hard to pull out.

senses.head: A large stiff feather, or a pen made from one
examples: A single quill had fallen out of the wing.
People used to write with goose quills.
The quill was stiff and hollow at the base.

senses.head: One of the sharp stiff spines on a porcupine
examples: The dog came home with quills in his nose.
A porcupine raises its quills when it feels threatened.
Each quill has a barbed tip that is hard to pull out.

entries.русский: маховое перо; гусиное перо (для письма); игла (дикобраза)

entries.meaning: The seasonal journey birds make from one region to another. ---
examples: The fall migration starts in late August.
Their yearly migration covers eight thousand miles.
Storms can throw whole migrations off course.

entries.meaning: Flight has 4 distinct senses.
examples: The owl's flight is completely silent.
We tracked the bird's flight until it went behind the trees.
A pelican's flight looks awkward until it hits the water.
Our flight was delayed three hours.
She booked a flight home for the holidays.
All flights out of the airport were canceled.
Her apartment is up two flights.
He carried the boxes up a flight of stairs.
